claims.text: The studied alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
The multi-principal-element composition governs the alloy's plastic strain and toughness under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
The multi-principal-element composition promotes solid-solution strengthening.
The multi-principal-element composition produces lattice distortion.
The multi-principal-element composition promotes formation of ductile phases.
Solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion impede dislocation motion in WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr contains ductile phases, potentially including Zr-rich regions.
The proposed ductile phases enhance energy absorption during deformation.
The combined strengthening, lattice-distortion, and ductile-phase mechanisms improve plastic strain and toughness.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain at failure than pure tungsten at 800–1200°C under otherwise identical tests.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten at 800–1200°C under otherwise identical tests.
Testing at 800–1200°C in vacuum or inert gas under tensile or fracture loading represents high-temperature plasma-facing-component service conditions.
The proposed scope is limited to 800–1200°C and may not extend to low-temperature or non-plasma-facing environments.
The relative contributions of solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, and ductile-phase formation are not quantified.
A controlled comparison will test as-fabricated WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten under identical high-temperature tensile and fracture-toughness conditions.
Failure of WTaTiVZr to exceed pure tungsten in both plastic strain and toughness would falsify the predicted performance advantage.
